Hi there,

I spent the last month moving every machine I own onto one SQLite file per device, and the most surprising part was how little of the work was about SQLite at all. Most of it was about deciding what a device is allowed to forget.

The first week went to the obvious parts: a change log per table, a clock per device and a merge that prefers the later write. That handled ninety percent of the cases and every one of the demos.

The second week went to deletes. A delete is the absence of a row, and an absence does not travel on its own. I tried three designs before settling on tombstones with a window measured in weeks, and I would skip the other two if I did it again.

The third and fourth weeks went to the slowest device in the house, an old tablet that comes online once a fortnight. It found every bug the others had hidden, and it is the reason the window is three weeks, not one.

If you are about to build something like this, start with the tablet.

Thanks for reading,
Sam
